description: Few-shot exemplars for non-code rep generation. One or two per type, hand-written to set the quality bar: concrete, reasoning-heavy, unambiguous, with a gradable rubric. Injected into the generation prompt as an example — never served directly.

design.prompt: A legal-tech team wants a chatbot over 50k contracts. Retrieval quality is poor: users get plausible-sounding but wrong clauses. Design your fix. Cover chunking, retrieval strategy, and how you'd prove it improved — and name the trade-offs you're accepting.

criteria.description: Diagnoses likely causes (chunking, embedding fit, no re-rank) before jumping to a fix
Proposes a concrete retrieval strategy (hybrid + re-rank) with reasons
Specifies how to prove improvement (labeled set, recall@k)

critique.prompt: Review this agent loop. Find every way it can misbehave in production, explain why each matters, and describe the fix.

criteria.description: Catches the unbounded loop (no step cap / termination)
Catches blind trust of tool name/args (KeyError, injection)
Gives concrete fixes, not just problem-spotting

explain.prompt: Explain what an embedding is to a backend engineer who's never used one. Cover what it represents, why 'similar meaning = close vectors' matters for search, and one thing beginners get wrong.
explain.audience: a backend engineer new to embeddings

criteria.description: Correctly explains embeddings as vectors capturing meaning
Connects vector similarity to retrieval/search usefully
Surfaces a real beginner misconception (e.g. keyword != semantic)
Precise, no hand-waving or jargon left undefined
